curated.instructions: omr/instructions/42040-1-1.pdf (book 1: the fire plane on floats, steps 1-50; the functions are photographed on page 115); omr/instructions/42040-1-2.pdf (book 2) builds the alternate model, a jet, whose functions are drawn on its pages 106-107

functions.does: Pushed along on the little wheels under its floats, the plane turns its propeller and engine: the front wheels' cross axle drives a 12 tooth bevel gear, a vertical shaft carries the turn up through the nose, and 12 tooth bevel gears at the top turn the crankshaft behind the propeller, so the pistons pump.
functions.source: book 1: the engine and its gears (steps 1-18 of the nose, pages 12-28), the floats and wheels (pages 28-36); inferred: that the wheels drive the propeller, the book draws no arrow
functions.note: unsure: by the model, the gears reach a 5.5 axle (p147 59426) behind the crankshaft but it is not clear how that couples to the crankshaft (p80 2853)

functions.does: The propeller turns the engine's crankshaft, and the pistons pump up and down in their cylinders.
functions.source: book 1: engine steps 1-18 (pages 12-22, the crankshaft drawn 1:1), steps 47-49 (propeller, pages 110-113)

functions.does: The hatch on top of the fuselage, behind the engine, flips forward to fill the tank with water (the eight clear blue bricks).
functions.note: unsure which parts form the hatch: the seat assembly's parts (p249-p265) sit behind the engine on top

functions.does: Pressing the knob on top of the fuselage drops the water: it pushes down a shaft that releases the tank's trapdoor in the belly, which swings open and lets the bricks fall out.
functions.source: book 1: page 115, picture 3 (the finger presses the knob, the door swings down, the water falls); the release shaft from the model
functions.note: the knob is pressed (a push of a few LDU down), not turned

functions.does: The trapdoor under the tank swings down by its own weight once released, and is pushed shut again by hand.
functions.skip: it falls open under gravity; worked by hand it just swings

functions.does: The red joystick on top behind the wing, tilted side to side, works the ailerons: its column turns knob wheels that turn the axles along the wing, and the axles tip the ailerons at the wing tips, one up and one down.
functions.source: book 1: the joystick and its knob wheels (pages 80-90), the wing's axles and ailerons (pages 90-108); inferred: what each tilt does, the book draws no arrows

functions.does: Tilted forward and back, the joystick works the elevator: a steering link under it pulls a lever at the tail, which tips the tailplane.
functions.source: book 1: the tail (pages 58-66), the joystick and link (pages 80-90); inferred: which way it goes

functions.does: The rudder on the fin swings side to side.
functions.source: book 1: the tail (pages 58-66); inferred: that it moves, and unsure whether anything works it

functions.does: The wheels under the floats roll.

questions.question: Do the float wheels drive the propeller, and what works the rudder?
